ledger.claim: Limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fails on the face of the trip record, so the baseline charge never gets off the ground. The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes the clause recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The clause is explicit that DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE is the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider, does not satisfy limb (d), and sends the trip to POL-NS-03. With limb (d) broken, the $4.00 is not chargeable under POL-NS-01 at all.

The GPS arrival test fails as well. The driver's trace carries 92 fixes across the whole 15 minute window and not one of them is a qualifying fix inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius: derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, and the driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 259.94 m from the Blk 118 pin. Under POL-NS-02 no qualifying in-radius fix exists in the 15 minutes preceding the cancellation, so the driver never arrived, POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails, and the rider is entitled to a full refund of the cancellation fee.

Dwell shortfall, stated in numbers as POL-NS-06 requires: the required minimum for STANDARD is 300 seconds and the effective in-geofence dwell is 0 seconds (longest_qualifying_run.duration_sec 0, run_count 0, shortfall 300 seconds). A dwell of zero against a 300 second minimum means the fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages.

Disclosure: EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and I cite it for its absence. No advisory covers Rivervale Drive in this window, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run in the driver's favour: limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a traffic_advisory is present and populated with a kerb-restriction, enforcement, closure or accident type, and the clause itself says a MISSING advisory makes the limb unavailable. The 300 second shortfall therefore stands unmodified.

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver — that he held position for the required dwell at some point outside the 50 m radius but inside the 400 m ceiling, his closest approach for the whole trip being 259.94 m — POL-NS-03 does not save the fee. On those facts the driver still did not arrive at the pickup point, POL-NS-01 limb (b) still fails, and POL-NS-03 refunds the cancellation fee to the rider in full. The only thing POL-NS-03 leaves open is the driver's compensation, and that is resolved against him below.

The pin-ambiguity escape is closed on this trip. POL-NS-03(ii) attributes a mislocation to pin ambiguity rather than to a party only where trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 2 or more; this trip records exactly 1 registered pickup point at the Blk 118 pin, so there is no platform-funded goodwill to allocate and no basis for calling this an ambiguous pin rather than a driver who stopped at the wrong block.

Fault under POL-NS-03(i) runs against the driver. The rider named the block in chat — 'im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark' — and the driver read that message at 07:22:30 and answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, so this is not a message he never saw. He nonetheless never moved to Blk 118: his closest approach in the entire trace is 259.94 m from that pin, and he cancelled at 07:33:05 without ever entering the arrival radius. A driver who is told the correct block, acknowledges it, and does not move to it before cancelling bears the loss and receives no compensation. Disclosure: the chat log EV-CHAT-00205 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.8 with issue code CONTENT_REDACTED; the redaction removed only the unit number, and the operative identifier 'blk 118' survives intact, so this claim survives the discount.

POL-NS-04 independently exonerates the rider. Limb (a): she sent a locating message during the waiting window, 'i dont see you at 118 leh' at 07:29:15, stating that she could not see the vehicle. Limb (b): the driver posted no reply to that message and trip_record.in_app_calls is empty, so no reply and no call came within 120 seconds of it or at all before he terminated the trip at 07:33:05; his earlier 'ok coming' answered the 07:22:10 message three minutes before he claimed to have arrived, not the locating message left hanging while he stood where she could not see him. Limb (c): the rider track is clean and places her device 96 qualifying fixes out of 96 with a maximum distance of 22.79 m from the pin, far inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius. Disclosure: EV-CHAT-00205 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.8 with issue code CONTENT_REDACTED, which does not touch the message text or timestamps this limb turns on. On POL-NS-04 the fee is refunded in full with no driver compensation payable.

This case is decidable on this record and no escalation limb is engaged on the profiles. rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1, well below the 3 that POL-NS-09(d) reads, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 against 104 completed trips, so neither the count limb nor the rate limb is met (2 is below 4, and 0.019 is far under 0.08). Both counterparts' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0. There is no basis to hold this fee away from the rider pending review.

On the remedy: this dispute was filed by the rider, the $4.00 cancellation fee is shown as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the amount reconciles with the fee schedule — STANDARD zone fee 4.00 against RYDE_X vehicle tier fee 4.00, the greater of the two being 4.00, so the charge line itself is not in dispute as to quantum. A ruling on POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03, POL-NS-04 or POL-NS-06 returns the whole of that $4.00 to the filing party as a FULL_REFUND, with amount_sgd of 4.00.

The rider cannot run this dispute through POL-NS-04, because limb (b) fails on the chat log's own timestamps. Limb (a) is met — the rider's 07:22:10 message names his block — but the driver sent MSG-00205-002 ('ok coming') at 07:22:48, 38 seconds later and far inside the 120 second window, so no finding of unanswered rider contact can be entered against the driver and limb (c) is never reached. Disclosure of impairment, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-CHAT-00205 carries weight_multiplier 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED (the unit number in MSG-00205-001 was redacted). The redaction removes no timestamp and no sender, so the 38 second interval this claim rests on is untouched by the discount.

The 4.00 fee cannot be carried by POL-NS-01, and the driver does not pretend otherwise. Limb (d) is excluded by the clause's own text because the trip terminated with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE; limb (b) fails because the driver's nearest approach to the pickup pin is 259.94 m against a 50 m STANDARD arrival radius; and limb (c) fails because the qualifying in-radius fix count is zero out of 92 driver fixes, leaving no in-geofence dwell to set against the 300 second minimum. This is exactly the case POL-NS-01 hands to POL-NS-03 — the category's clause for an honest mislocation rather than a manufactured no-show — and the dispute is to be reasoned there, not on the baseline clause.

What the record does establish is an honest wrong-block attempt, and that distinction should be written into the ruling. The trip record computes a wait_time_min of 6.4 running from the arrived event at 07:26:40 to the cancellation at 07:33:05: the driver gave the rider six and a half minutes rather than harvesting a fee. His closest approach to the pin is 259.94 m — inside POL-NS-03's 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling and inside POL-NS-05's 300 m line. POL-NS-05 catches only an arrival fix that puts the driver more than 300 m out, or in motion at 15 kph or above, at the arrived timestamp; the published derived facts key no distance and no speed to that timestamp, and the only distance they publish sits inside the 300 m line, so the false-marker limb is not made out. This trip therefore belongs to the wrong-entrance route POL-NS-05's closing sentence preserves, and it should not be recorded as a false-arrival event against the driver.

Two points are closed against the driver on this record and the driver does not stretch them. First, the pin-ambiguity limb of POL-NS-03(ii) requires trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more; this trip records one registered pickup point, so the platform-funded goodwill of 50 per cent — 2.00 against the 4.00 fee — is unavailable and the derived goodwill figure has nothing to attach to. Second, the rider did name the block, MSG-00205-001 reading 'im at blk 118', with the redaction removing only the unit number, so under POL-NS-03(i) the residual loss sits with the driver and no compensation is payable to him. The chat artifact is impaired at weight 0.8 on issue CONTENT_REDACTED, which is why the surviving block identifier, and not the redacted unit number, is the fact relied on.

The sum charged is not open to attack on integrity grounds, and no partial refund can be built on it. The fare breakdown carries a single cancellation-fee line of 4.00 SGD, and 4.00 is exactly the greater of the two schedule figures this trip attracts — the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00, the schedule dimension resolving to a tie — so the line reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule and no limb of POL-NS-08(d) is engaged on this trip.

There is no fee-farming pattern behind this cancelled trip. On the two fields POL-NS-07 names, and no others, driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2, below the 4 the clause requires, and 2 over driver_profile.completed_trips_30d of 104 is a rate of 0.019, below the 0.08 the clause also requires: the anti-farming test fails on both limbs, so nothing on the driver's 30-day record supports an adverse inference. On the rider side, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 against POL-NS-09(d)'s threshold of 3, and the counterparty-dispute counts are 0 and 0 against POL-NS-09(c)'s threshold of 2. Under POL-GEN-01 every other entry on either profile — rating, acceptance rate, lifetime counters — is context only and can ground nothing.

ledger.claim: In the alternative, and only if the Judge is not prepared to run the wrong-entrance findings, this case should be escalated rather than guessed at. The trip record and the trace contradict each other directly on arrival and dwell: the record enters an arrived event at 07:26:40 with a 6.4 minute wait, while the 92 driver fixes never come closer to the pin than 259.94 m and show zero in-geofence dwell. The published derived facts key neither a distance nor a speed to the arrived timestamp, so POL-NS-05 cannot be run (its condition needs a fix more than 300 m out or at 15 kph at that timestamp) and POL-NS-03 cannot be run either (its condition needs a stationary hold within 400 m). That head-on conflict between two admissible artifacts is what POL-NS-09(b) exists for, and under POL-GEN-03 the consequence is a terminal escalation with the disputed 4.00 held rather than refunded.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: the $4.00 cancellation fee on this trip is refunded in full to the rider. The driver never reached the pickup point. The GPS trace carries 92 driver fixes across the whole window and not one of them falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius (qualifying in-geofence fixes: 0); the driver's closest approach for the entire trip is 259.94 m from the Blk 118 pin. POL-NS-01 therefore fails on three separate limbs and the baseline charge never attaches: no in-geofence arrival (limb b), no in-geofence dwell to set against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (limb c), and a trip closed by the driver with reason code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which limb (d) expressly excludes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. POL-NS-02 gives the rider the full refund on that finding, and on the wrong-block route — the driver did hold position roughly 260 m away, inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling — POL-NS-03 refunds the fee in full as well. POL-NS-06 independently produces the same arithmetic: required dwell 300 s, effective in-geofence dwell 0 s, shortfall 300 s. The fee line itself is not attacked: 4.00 SGD is the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee (4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (4.00), a tie, so the fare breakdown reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule and POL-NS-08(d) is not engaged.

Driver compensation is nil. POL-NS-01 is not satisfied, so POL-NS-07 never engages. Under POL-NS-03 the fault allocation runs against you, driver: the rider named the block in chat ('im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark'), you read it at 07:22:30 and answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48, and your trace never comes closer than 259.94 m to that pin before you cancelled at 07:33:05. The pin-ambiguity goodwill route is closed on the same facts: POL-NS-03(ii) needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more to attribute the mislocation to the platform, and this trip records exactly 1, so the 50 per cent figure (2.00) has nothing to attach to. Your 6.4-minute wait also cannot help you: it runs from your own arrival tap, and POL-NS-01(c) measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from that event — there is no qualifying fix at all, so the measured dwell is zero.

The request in the alternative for a terminal escalation is refused. The trip record's arrival event and the GPS trace do not leave an unresolved conflict for POL-NS-09(b): POL-NS-01(c) and POL-NS-05 make an arrival tap a status the driver set rather than proof of arrival, and POL-NS-03 is the named clause that decides a driver who is at the wrong face of the pickup — your 259.94 m closest approach sits inside its 400 m ceiling, which is the wrong-entrance case, not the 800 m example POL-NS-09(b) describes. No false-arrival referral is recorded against you either: the published GPS facts key no distance and no speed to the 07:26:40 arrival timestamp, and the closest approach of 259.94 m is inside POL-NS-05's 300 m line, so the false-marker limb is not established. EV-ADVIS-00205-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0) and is cited only for its absence: with no populated advisory, POL-NS-06(i) cannot be used to sum separate intervals, and the 300-second shortfall stands.

On integrity and weight: EV-CHAT-00205 is impaired at weight 0.80 with issue CONTENT_REDACTED (the unit number in the rider's first message). The finding that the rider named the block survives that discount, because the operative identifier 'blk 118' is intact and the redaction touches no message text, sender or timestamp this case turns on; in any event the refund does not rest on the chat log. The deciding facts — zero qualifying in-geofence fixes, zero dwell, and the DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE code — are carried by EV-GPS-00205 and EV-TRIP-00205, both at weight 1.00, so confidence is capped at 1.00 and no escalation floor is crossed. On the profiles, nothing supports escalation: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 2 (below 4) and 2 over 104 completed trips is 0.019 (below 0.08), the anti-farming check fails on both limbs, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), and both counterparty-dispute counts are 0 (below 2). Every other profile entry is context only and grounds nothing. The rider's alternative POL-NS-04 route, and the driver's answer that the 07:22:48 reply defeats limb (b), are noted but need not be resolved: the full refund is established independently by POL-NS-02, POL-NS-03 and POL-NS-06 and is the same either way. Result: the $4.00 charged fee is returned to the rider in full, no compensation is payable to the driver, and no referral is made.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
